page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). It features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server includes 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a high density of 16.0 GB per vCPU. It does not provide bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote managed disks for non-volatile storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates balanced single-core computation alongside constrained parallel throughput due to the 4 vCPU topology. Single-thread processing registers within the average range, scoring 1610.0 in Geekbench single-core, 1897.09 in stress-ng single-core, and achieving 28.48 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show weak output, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 3462.0, a PassMark CPU score of 5927.41, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 3876.57. Memory bandwidth tests yield 28.43 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 24.5 GB/sec for write operations, matching the performance envelope of a constrained vCPU allocation on a larger physical socket.

The primary operational advantage of the E8-4s_v5 is its memory-to-vCPU ratio. By allocating 64 GB of memory to only 4 vCPUs, it is structurally optimized to reduce per-core software licensing expenditures while maintaining a substantial RAM allocation. Its application performance profiles indicate 3.85 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 6.19 GB/sec throughput in static web serving. These characteristics make the instance best suited for memory-intensive production databases, large in-memory caches, and enterprise data processing tasks that do not require intensive multi-threaded CPU compute.

The system provides 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores and is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated ratio of 16.0 GB of memory per core. It contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for disk persistence. In performance evaluations, the instance demonstrates average single-core CPU metrics but weak multi-core throughput due to its low vCPU count. Its memory bandwidth achieves 28.43 GB/sec on large read blocks. The E8-4s_v5 delivers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations facing per-core software licensing constraints, making it suited for memory-heavy enterprise databases, Redis caching layers, and moderate-throughput backend services requiring large working memory sets.
